ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p160/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p160/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p160/r4.claim: The oath bears witness that the Qur’an is exalted revelation from God, kept in a protected book and accessible only to pure, near angels, never to jinn or devils.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p160/r4.anchor: It is found in a protected book with the Almighty and no one except His pure angels can have access to it

QASHANI:56:73-82/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:56:73-82/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:56:73-82/r5.claim: The noble Qur’an is exalted, ancient, honorable comprehensive knowledge; its hidden book is the Prophet’s heart, where Qur’anic intellect is deposited beyond the senses except for purified angels.
QASHANI:56:73-82/r5.anchor: هو قلبه المكنون في الغيب عن الحواس وما عدا المقربين من الملائكة المطهرين

QASHANI:56:73-82/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:56:73-82/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:56:73-82/r6.claim: The hidden book may instead be the first Spirit, locus of decree and abode of the Muhammadan Spirit, or the Muhammadan Spirit itself.
QASHANI:56:73-82/r6.anchor: أو الروح الأول الذي هو محل القضاء ومأوى الروح المحمدي، بل هو هو

QASHANI:56:73-82/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:56:73-82/r7.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
QASHANI:56:73-82/r7.claim: Jesus says knowledge is not brought down from heaven, raised from earth, or carried across seas; it is placed in hearts and appears through spiritual manners before God.
QASHANI:56:73-82/r7.anchor: لا تقولوا العلم في السماء من ينزل به، ولا في تخوم الأرض من يصعد به

QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r7.claim: The hidden book is identified as the Preserved Tablet or written copies, and is protected from alteration.
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r7.anchor: في اللوح المحفوظ . ويقال : في المصاحف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r10.claim: A maknūn book is protected; Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify it as the heavenly book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r10.anchor: في كتاب مكنون: أي مصون. قال ابن عباس ومجاهد: الكتاب الذي في السماء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r11.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r11.claim: ʿIkrima takes the hidden book as the Torah and Gospel, where the Qurʾān’s honor is mentioned, making the verse appeal to prior revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r11.anchor: وقال عكرمة: التوراة والإنجيل، كأنه قال: ذكر في كتاب مكنون كرمه وشرفه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r12.claim: Another view takes the protected book as Muslims’ safeguarded codices; since codices did not yet exist, this would be a prediction of the unseen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p92/r12.anchor: وقيل: في كتاب مكنون: أي في مصاحف للمسلمين مصونة من التبديل والتغيير،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p22#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p22#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p22#2/r3.claim: The hidden book is the Preserved Tablet with God, protected from devils.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p22#2/r3.anchor: في اللوح المحفوظ، محفوظ من الشياطين

BAYDAWI-FULL:56:76-79/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:76-79/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:76-79/r4.claim: The protected book is the Preserved Tablet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:76-79/r4.anchor: { فى كتب مكنون } مصون وهو اللوح المحفوظ

NAHHAS:v4p341/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p341/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p341/r16.claim: The referent is protected and guarded.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r8.claim: “In a hidden book” is an honorific metaphor, not literal description; the preposition “in” marks figurative containment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r8.anchor: فليس لفظ { كتاب } ولا وصف { مكنون } مرادا بهما الحقيقة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r5.claim: They take the protected book as the book in heaven; ʿIkrima instead says it means the Torah and Gospel, making the Quran's honor attested in prior revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ومجاهد: أراد الكتاب الذي في السماء. وقال عكرمة: أراد التوراة والإنجيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r6.claim: Other interpreters take it as Muslim codices, making the verse a report of the unseen before those codices existed; its protection lasts to Resurrection, and touch may refer to manuscripts or metaphorically to angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p251/r6.anchor: وقال بعض المتأولين: أراد مصاحف المسلمين، وكانت يوم نزلت الآية لم تكن، فهي على هذا إخبار بغيب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r8.claim: The Qur'an is noble—excellent in its kind, beneficial, or honored by God—and the protected book is inaccessible to all but purified angels if it means the Preserved Tablet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r8.anchor: كريم حسن مرضي في جنسه من الكتب . أو نفاع جم المنافع . أو كريم على الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r9.claim: If the protected book describes the Qur'an, only a person ritually pure should touch its written copy; some extend this to recitation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p466/r9.anchor: وإن جعلتها صفة للقرآن ؛ فالمعنى لا ينبغي أن يمسه إلا من هو على الطهارة من الناس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r15.claim: The guarded book is the Preserved Tablet in heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r15.anchor: أنه كتاب في السماء وهو اللوح المحفوظ

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r16.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r16.claim: Alternatively, it is the Torah and Gospel, which mention the Qur'an and its messenger.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r16.anchor: التوراة والإنجيل فيهما ذكر القرآن وذكر من ينزل عليه ، قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r17.claim: Another view identifies it as the Psalms.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r18.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r18.claim: It may be the written Qur'an in people's hands.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r20.speaker: يعقوب عن مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r20.claim: It may mean guarded against falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r20.anchor: محفوظ عن الباطل , قاله يعقوب بن مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p462/r21.claim: A further possibility is that its meanings are concealed within it.

MUQATIL:56:74-82/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:56:74-82/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:56:74-82/r6.claim: The protected book is hidden from creation in the Preserved Tablet at God's right hand by the Throne.
MUQATIL:56:74-82/r6.anchor: { في كتاب مكنون } [آية: 78] يعنى مستور من خلقه، عند الله في اللوح المحفوظ عن يمين العرش

TABATABAI:56:75-80/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r8.claim: The hidden book means the Preserved Tablet, protecting the Qur'an from alteration or replacement.
TABATABAI:56:75-80/r8.anchor: وهو اللوح المحفوظ كما قال تعالى بل هو قرآن مجيد في لوح محفوظ

THALABI:v9p218/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p218/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p218/r5.claim: The hidden book is protected with God from devils and from anything that could stain it.
THALABI:v9p218/r5.anchor: في كتاب مكنون مصون. عند الله سبحانه محفوظ عن الشياطين وعن جميع ما يشين.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:75/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:75/r7.speaker: Müfessirlerin birçoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:75/r7.claim: Many exegetes favor “the preserved book” as the Preserved Tablet, a spiritual description expressing the Qur'an's exalted status.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:75/r7.anchor: birçok müfessir tarafından güçlü bulunan yoruma göre buradaki “kitap” kelimesinden maksat “levh-i mahfûz”dur

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r2.claim: Verses 75–96 signal the Qur’an’s exalted status and its protection from Satan and his agents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r2.anchor: it is above and beyond the reach of Satan and his agents

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r3.claim: Quraysh are cautioned not to ignore the sublime message and thereby bring doom upon themselves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p136/r3.anchor: not to turn a deaf ear to this sublime message and invite their doom

BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r3.claim: The hidden book is fixed and protected because of its preciousness, in the Preserved Tablet, in honored hearts, and in purified, honored codices, safe from alteration.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p425/r3.anchor: في السماء في اللوح المحفوظ , وفي الأرض في الصدور المشرفة , وفي السطور في المصاحف المكرمة المطهرة

JISHUMI:v9p6768/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6768/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6768/r6.claim: Calling the Quran a discourse, revelation, and guarded book, and saying it is not touched, shows it is originated rather than eternal, since these descriptions fit neither literal nor figurative eternity.
JISHUMI:v9p6768/r6.anchor: وتدل على حدث القرآن؛ لأنه وصفه بأنه حديث وتنزيل، وكتاب مكنون، ولا يمسه

TABRISI:56:83/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:83/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:56:83/r16.claim: The hidden, guarded Book is the Preserved Tablet in which God recorded the Qur’an.
TABRISI:56:83/r16.anchor: { في كتاب مكنون } أي مستور من خلقه عند الله وهو اللوح المحفوظ أثبت الله فيه القرآن عن ابن عباس.

TABRISI:56:83/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:83/r17.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:56:83/r17.claim: Another interpretation identifies the hidden Book as the codex in people’s hands.
TABRISI:56:83/r17.anchor: هو المصحف الذي في أيدينا عن مجاهد.

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r8.claim: One reading takes the Qurʾān itself as being in a book, namely the Preserved Tablet.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r8.anchor: فكذلك ههنا أن القرآن كريم وهو في كتاب

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r9.claim: A related reading takes noble as its quality in the book: the Qurʾān is noble in the Preserved Tablet even if disbelievers do not regard it as noble.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r9.anchor: فالقرآن كريم في اللوح المحفوظ وإن لم يكن كريما عند الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r10.claim: Another reading makes the whole description Qurʾān noble the content written in the book, as in the statement about ʿIlliyyūn.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r10.anchor: والمراد حينئذ أنه في اللوح المحفوظ

RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r11.claim: All these readings are sound, but the first most strongly honors the heavenly recited text.
RAZI-FULL:v29p166/r11.anchor: والأول أبلغ في التعظيم بالمقروء السماوي

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r1.claim: The book is most correctly identified as the Preserved Tablet, supported by 85:21–22.

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r2.claim: A second view identifies the book as the codex.

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r3.claim: A third view identifies it as an earlier revealed scripture, so the Qurʾān is also found in the Torah, Gospel, and other scriptures.
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r3.anchor: كتاب من الكتب المنزلة فهو قرآن في التوراة

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r4.claim: Although the word's pattern raises an objection, a tablet whose function is to receive writing can itself be called a book, as with words for a covering or a storage chest.
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r4.anchor: اللوح لما لم يكن إلا الذي يكتب فيه صح تسميته كتابا

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r5.claim: Maknūn means perfectly protected; concealment is the attendant of the highest protection, since what is precious is hidden from sight.

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r6.claim: Alternatively, the Tablet is literally hidden from sight except for selected angels, while the written Qurʾān is protected from alteration and corrupting hands.
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r6.anchor: اللوح المحفوظ مستور عن العين لا يطلع عليه إلا ملائكة مخصوصون

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r7.claim: The book answers those who said the recitation came from jinn: the angel received it from a book before delivering it, so it is not even angelic speech, much less jinn speech.
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r7.anchor: لم ينزل به عليه الملك إلا بعدما أخذه من كتاب فهو ليس بكلام الملائكة فضلا أن يكون كلام الجن

RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r8.claim: Maknūn answers the claim that it is ancient lore in open books: it is concealed, and only the purified touch it.
RAZI-FULL:v29p167/r8.anchor: لا بل هو { في كتاب مكنون * لا يمسه إلا المطهرون }

STUDYQURAN:56:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:78/r1.speaker: Aj, Q, R, Sh, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:56:78/r1.claim: Most take the concealed Book as the Preserved Tablet, said to contain every revealed book; 85:22 is cited.
STUDYQURAN:56:78/r1.anchor: Book is taken by most to mean the Preserved Tablet (85:22; Aj, Q, R, Sh, Ṭ), which is said to contain all of the books of revelation.

STUDYQURAN:56:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:78/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:56:78/r2.claim: The Quran's nobility and concealment signify its preservation from influence by anyone but God, refuting claims that it is jinn's whispering or ancient fables; the commentary cites 6:25, 8:31, 16:24, 23:83, 25:5, 27:68, 46:17, 68:15, and 83:13.
STUDYQURAN:56:78/r2.anchor: That it is both noble and concealed indicates that the Quran is preserved from the influence of anyone but God

TAB-FULL:v22p363/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r1.claim: The verse refers to a guarded book with God, protected from harm such as dust.
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {في كتاب مكنون} [الواقعة: 78] قال: «القرآن في كتابه المكنون الذي لا يمسه شيء من تراب ولا غبار»

TAB-FULL:v22p363/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the Qur’an is in its hidden book, untouched by earth or dust.
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {في كتاب مكنون} [الواقعة: 78] قال: «القرآن في كتابه المكنون الذي لا يمسه شيء من تراب ولا غبار»

TAB-FULL:v22p363/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r5.speaker: جابر بن زيد وأبي نهيك
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r5.claim: Jābir ibn Zayd and Abū Nuhayk say the hidden book is in heaven.
TAB-FULL:v22p363/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن زيد، وأبي نهيك، في قوله: {في كتاب مكنون} [الواقعة: 78] قال: «هو كتاب في السماء»

TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2.claim: Other verses depict the Qur'an as preserved in a guarded tablet, an exalted wise source, and a protected book; its meanings rest on enduring, unchanging realities.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2.anchor: فهذه الآيات ونظائرها تحكي عن إتكاء القرآن في معانيه على حقائق ثابتة غير متغيرة ولا متغير ما يتكي عليها

BURSEVI:v9p275/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p275/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p275/r1.claim: The hidden Book is the Preserved Tablet, protected from access by all except the angels brought near to God.
BURSEVI:v9p275/r1.anchor: أي مصون عن غير المقربين من الملائكة أي لا يطلع عليه من سواهم وهو اللوح المحفوظ

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:77-78/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:77-78/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:77-78/r2.claim: It is kept protected with God in a guarded book.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:77-78/r2.anchor: { في كتاب مكنون } مصون عند الله.

BURHAN:v2p28/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p28/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p28/r1.claim: Zarkashi notes that many scholars composed works on abrogation, naming Qatada, Abu Ubayd, Abu Dawud, al-Nahhas, Ibn al-Jawzi, and others.
BURHAN:v2p28/r1.anchor: وقد صنف فيه جماعة كثيرون منهم قتادة بن دعامة ( 1 ) السدوسي وأبو عبيد

BURHAN:v2p28/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p28/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p28/r4.claim: The imams require anyone interpreting the Qur'an to know which passages abrogate and which are abrogated.
BURHAN:v2p28/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز لأحد أن يفسر كتاب الله إلا بعد أن يعرف منه الناسخ والمنسوخ

BURHAN:v2p28/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p28/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BURHAN:v2p28/r5.claim: Ali asked a preacher whether he knew abrogation; when the man answered that God knew best, Ali said he had perished and led others to ruin.
BURHAN:v2p28/r5.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب لقاص أتعرف الناسخ والمنسوخ قال الله أعلم قال هلكت وأهلكت

BURHAN:v2p28/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p28/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p28/r8.claim: Naskh is also used for transfer, as in transferring an inheritance from one person to another.
BURHAN:v2p28/r8.anchor: وبمعنى التحويل كتناسخ المواريث يعني تحويل الميراث من واحد إلى واحد

BURHAN:v2p28/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p28/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله محمد بن بركات السعدي
BURHAN:v2p28/r11.claim: Ibn Barakat al-Saʿdi supports al-Nahhas's copying sense with the Qur'an's record of deeds and the revelation's preservation in the Mother Book and a guarded book.
BURHAN:v2p28/r11.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو عبد الله محمد بن بركات السعدي يشهد ( 4 ) لما قاله النحاس

BURHAN:v1p276/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p276/r1.claim: كتاب derives from writing, whose root sense is gathering; the Qur'an gathers stories, verses, rulings, and reports in an ordered form, while “book” for the written object is metaphorical.
BURHAN:v1p276/r1.anchor: وأصلها الجمع وسميت الكتابة لجمعها الحروف فاشتق الكتاب لذلك لأنه يجمع أنواعا من القصص والآيات والأحكام والأخبار

BURHAN:v1p276/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p276/r2.claim: The “hidden book” in 56:78 is the Preserved Tablet.
BURHAN:v1p276/r2.anchor: ﴿ في كتاب مكنون ﴾ أى اللوح المحفوظ

BURHAN:v1p276/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p276/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p276/r3.claim: Writing consists of arranged lines on a medium that signify intended meaning, though a writer may err and produce marks that signify nothing.
BURHAN:v1p276/r3.anchor: والكتابة حركات تقوم بمحل قدرة الكاتب خطوط موضوعة مجتمعة تدل على المعنى المقصود وقد يغلط الكاتب فلا تدل على شىء

ITQAN:v1p143/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p143/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p143/r2.claim: The Qur’an is called a Book because it gathers sciences, stories, and reports in the most eloquent form; kitab linguistically means gathering.
ITQAN:v1p143/r2.anchor: فأما تسميته كتابا فلجمعه أنواع العلوم والقصص والأخبار على أبلغ وجه

ITQAN:v3p55/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p55/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p55/r1.claim: The science of abrogation was treated in many dedicated works, including books by Abu Ubayd, Abu Dawud al-Sijistani, al-Nahhas, Ibn al-Anbari, Makki, and Ibn al-Arabi.
ITQAN:v3p55/r1.anchor: أفرده بالتصنيف خلائق لا يحصون منهم أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام وأبو داود السجستاني

ITQAN:v3p55/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p55/r2.speaker: الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p55/r2.claim: The leading scholars say no one may interpret God’s Book before learning abrogating and abrogated passages.
ITQAN:v3p55/r2.anchor: قال الأئمة لا يجوز لأحد أن يفسر كتاب الله إلا بعد أن يعرف منه الناسخ والمنسوخ

ITQAN:v3p55/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p55/r3.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v3p55/r3.claim: Ali told a judge who did not know abrogation that he was doomed and would doom others.
ITQAN:v3p55/r3.anchor: وقد قال علي لقاض أتعرف الناسخ من المنسوخ قال لا قال هلكت وأهلكت

ITQAN:v3p55/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p55/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p55/r4.claim: Naskh can mean removal, replacement, transformation such as inheritance passing between heirs, or transcription from one place to another.
ITQAN:v3p55/r4.anchor: يرد النسخ بمعنى الإزالة ومنه قوله

ITQAN:v3p55/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p55/r5.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v3p55/r5.claim: Makki rejects transcription or copying as a Qur’anic sense of naskh: the abrogating passage does not reproduce the abrogated wording but uses different wording.
ITQAN:v3p55/r5.anchor: قال مكي وهذا الوجه لا يصح أن يكون في القرآن وأنكر على النحاس إجازته ذلك

ITQAN:v3p55/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p55/r6.speaker: السعيدي
ITQAN:v3p55/r6.claim: Al-Sa‘idi supports al-Nahhas’s transcription sense with verses about recording deeds and the Mother Book; all revelation is in the Preserved Tablet, as 56:78 says.
ITQAN:v3p55/r6.anchor: ومعلوم أن ما نزل من الوحي نجوما جميعه في أم الكتاب وهو اللوح المحفوظ

ITQAN:v3p55/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p55/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p55/r7.claim: Abrogation is a dispensation distinctive to this community, accepted by Muslims for facilitation; Jews wrongly equate it with a change in divine knowledge, though it only specifies a ruling’s duration, like changing states of life, health, and wealth.
ITQAN:v3p55/r7.anchor: وأنكره اليهود ظنا منهم أنه بداء كالذي يرى الرأي ثم يبدو له وهو باطل لأنه بيان مدة الحكم

ITQAN:v3p55/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p55/r8.speaker: قوم من العلماء
ITQAN:v3p55/r8.claim: Some scholars hold that only Qur’an can abrogate Qur’an, citing the promise of a better or equal replacement and arguing that only Qur’an can match or surpass it.
ITQAN:v3p55/r8.anchor: واختلف العلماء فقيل لا ينسخ القرآن إلا بقرآن

ZAJJAJ:v5p115#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p115#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p115#2/r1.claim: The guarded book is in heaven, in the Preserved Tablet.
ZAJJAJ:v5p115#2/r1.anchor: أي مصون في السماء في اللوح المحفوظ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p954/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p954/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p954/r3.claim: The angelic referent strengthens the view that the guarded book is the preserved tablet, rather than the Quran as available to people.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p954/r3.anchor: هذا المعنى يقوّي القول أن المقصود في الآية الكتاب المكنون الذي هو في اللوح المحفوظ وليس القرآن الذي بين أيدينا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r1.claim: The hidden book is the Preserved Tablet, inaccessible to all except the angels brought near.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r1.anchor: فالمراد به اللوح المحفوظ كما روي عن الربيع بن أنس وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r2.claim: The book is the Muslim codex, protected from alteration; this also implies foreknowledge because the Qur’an was then in written codices.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : أي في كتاب مصون عن التبديل والتغيير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r3.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r3.claim: Ikrima, as cited by Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir, identifies the book as the Torah and Gospel.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن عكرمة أنه قال : في كتاب أي التوراة والإنجيل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r4.claim: Al-Bahr explains the phrase as saying that the Qur’an’s honor and nobility are mentioned in a hidden book; this requires book to mean the general class of revealed books.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r4.anchor: وحكى ذلك في البحر ثم قال : كأنه قال : ذكر في كتاب مكنون كرمه وشرفه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r5.claim: If Torah and Gospel are intended, book must be generic; hiddenness may figuratively denote lofty rank, since concealment accompanies what is exalted.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r5.anchor: والظاهر أنه أريد على هذا بالكتاب الجنس لتصح إرادة التوراة والإنجيل وفي وصف ذلك بالمكنون خفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r6.claim: An alternative says the hidden book is the heart of the believer; al-Alusi dismisses this suggestion.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r6.anchor: وقيل : الكتاب المكنون قلب المؤمن وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r7.claim: The interpretation that the book is only protected from alteration cites 15:9, but al-Alusi prefers the earlier explanations, especially the Preserved Tablet.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r7.anchor: وقيل : المراد من كونه في كتاب مكنون كونه محفوظا من التغيير والتبديل ليس إلا كما قال تعالى : ( وإنا له لحافظون ) والمعول عليه ما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r8.claim: The prepositional phrase may modify كريم, meaning the Qur’an is noble in the Preserved Tablet even if unbelievers do not regard it as noble; the adjectival reading is more eloquent.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#3/r8.anchor: وجوز تعلق الجار بكريم كما يقال زيد كريم في نفسه والمعنى إنه كريم في اللوح المحفوظ

DURR-FULL:v8p27/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p27/r1.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
DURR-FULL:v8p27/r1.claim: Salman says the hidden Book is in heaven and touched only by angels; he then recited whatever Qur'an his visitors wished.
DURR-FULL:v8p27/r1.anchor: عن علقمة رضي الله عنه قال: أتينا سلمان الفارسي رضي الله عنه فخرج علينا

DURR-FULL:v8p27/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p27/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p27/r2.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains the hidden Book as in heaven and the purified as angels.
DURR-FULL:v8p27/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله: {في كتاب مكنون} قال: في السماء {لا يمسه إلا المطهرون} قال: الملائكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r1.claim: The hidden book is a metaphor for the correspondence of the Quran’s wording and meanings with God’s knowledge, will, and command to the angel who conveyed it; these matters are concealed from people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r1.anchor: أي محجوب عن أنظار الناس فهو أمر مغيب لا يعلم كنهه إلا الله .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r2.claim: The Quran heard from the Prophet matches what God intended to communicate and the miraculous arrangement He willed to create, confirming it as divine speech rather than human composition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r2.anchor: أن القرآن الذي بلغهم وسمعوه من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو موافق لما أراد الله إعلام الناس به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r3.claim: The locative is borrowed to express correspondence, like a container’s contents matching its container; this is better than treating the Quran’s description as a rational-metonymic attribution of its counterpart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r3.anchor: فاستعير حرف الظرفية لمعنى مطابقة ما هو عند الله ، تشبيها لتلك المطابقة باتحاد المظروف بالظرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r4.claim: Book is also a metaphor for a fixed, unalterable reality; combined with the locative metaphor, it expresses the Quran’s meanings matching God’s knowledge, will, and power and its words matching the divinely created eloquent discourse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r4.anchor: واستعير الكتاب للأمر الثابت المحقق الذي لا يقبل التغيير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites a poetic fragment as a parallel for using book to signify an established matter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p333/r5.anchor: وقريب من هذه الاستعارة قول بشر بن أبي حازم أو الطرماح : وجدنا في كتاب بني تميم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the protected book as the Preserved Tablet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه اللوح المحفوظ قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r2.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda identify it as the written Qur’an in our hands.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه المصحف الذي بأيدينا قاله مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r3.claim: On the Preserved Tablet interpretation, Muqātil says maknūn means hidden from creatures.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r3.anchor: أحدهما مستور عن الخلق قاله مقاتل وهذا على القول الأول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p151#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says maknūn means protected or preserved.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r2.claim: The Quran is exalted in a book that is itself exalted, guarded, and honored.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r2.anchor: أي: معظم في كتاب معظم محفوظ موقر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the concealed book as the book in heaven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p544/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {لا يمسه إلا المطهرون} قال: الكتاب الذي في السماء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#3/r1.claim: The book is the Preserved Tablet.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ في كتاب ﴾ أي اللوح المحفوظ ﴿ مكنون ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#3/r2.claim: Maknūn means protected from falsehood or concealed from those other than the angels brought near, so no one else can view it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p212#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ مكنون ﴾ مصون عن أن يأتيه الباطل أو من غير المقربين من الملائكة

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r6.claim: The hidden book is protected with God; another explanation says it is guarded from falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r6.anchor: مصون عند الله تعالى. وقيل: مكنون محفوظ عن الباطل.

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the book is in heaven.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r7.anchor: والكتاب هنا كتاب في السماء قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r8.speaker: جابر بن زيد وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r8.claim: Jābir ibn Zayd and Ibn ʿAbbās identify the hidden book as the Preserved Tablet.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r8.anchor: وقال جابر بن زيد وابن عباس أيضا: هو اللوح المحفوظ.

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r9.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r9.claim: ʿIkrima says it is the Torah and Gospel, which mention the Qur'an and the one to whom it will be sent.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r9.anchor: عكرمة: التوراة والإنجيل فيهما ذكر القرآن ومن ينزل عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r10.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r10.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the book as the Psalms.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r10.anchor: السدي: الزبور. مجاهد وقتادة: هو المصحف

QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r11.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r11.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say it is the codex in people's hands.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:77-79/r11.anchor: مجاهد وقتادة: هو المصحف الذي في أيدينا.
